page: Amazon Web Services m9g.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 48 dedicated physical cores based on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieved top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression (36.49 GB/sec) and both single- and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (17.39 GB/sec and 624.06 GB/sec, respectively). Passmark memory and database operations benchmarks also ranked in the top tier, alongside Redis SET operations reaching 136.27 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 97.07 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Passmark physics tests registered as strong, while single-core CPU performance and LLM inference speeds for 135M and 7B models remained in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m9g.12xlarge offers high resource density and strong memory bandwidth relative to its ARM64 hardware class, making it efficient for scale-out workloads. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU accelerators represents a tradeoff for applications requiring high-speed local caching or heavy parallel computing. The instance is suited for workloads such as database operations, high-throughput web serving, caching layers like Redis, and multi-threaded data compression tasks.
